name: apply 1b — catch-up: fetch applications and decisions the webhook missed

nodes.name: Sweep schedule
nodes.notes: Cadence comes from SWEEP_CRON (daily in production). The sweep is the backstop for missed or failed webhook deliveries: it re-syncs pending applications and re-checks decisions. Everything it does is idempotent, so overlapping with the webhook is safe.

nodes.name: Fetch pending applications
nodes.notes: Host.hostApplications requires host-admin auth: credential 'oc-host-admin' (Header Auth, header name Personal-Token) — select it here once the operator has created it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query($h:String){host(slug:$h){slug hostApplications(limit:50,status:PENDING,orderBy:{field:CREATED_AT,direction:DESC}){totalCount nodes{createdAt message customData account{slug name description longDescription socialLinks{type url} members(role:ADMIN,limit:10){nodes{account{... on Individual{email} } } } } } } } }', variables: { h: $json.host_slug } }) }}

nodes.name: Only new slugs
nodes.notes: Idempotency: existing rows pass through untouched, so a sweep can never pull a row back to an earlier stage.

nodes.name: Still open?
nodes.notes: Terminal rows are dropped: a decision already recorded is never re-recorded and never re-emailed.

nodes.name: Fetch application status
nodes.notes: Public account fields, readable by any token. hostApplicationRequests was used here until 2026-10-01 and demands admin of the applicant collective, which a host-admin token is not.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query($s:String){account(slug:$s){slug ... on AccountWithHost{isApproved approvedAt host{slug} } } }', variables: { s: $json.slug } }) }}

nodes.name: Render decision email
nodes.notes: DRY_RUN is checked here, at the send site: when true the message goes to DRY_RUN_RECIPIENT with the intended recipient named in the subject. Templates embedded verbatim from automation/emails/decision-*.md.

Ask apply 2 to review now

workflowId.cachedResultName: apply 2 — AI review: advisory first read of every new application

nodes.notes: Only the path that creates rows hands off, and only after the Slack thread anchor is stored, so the review has a thread to reply in. Fire and forget: it never waits and it never fails this workflow. apply 2 reads the rows itself, so nothing is passed, and its own schedule still covers a hand-off that is lost. The decision branch is untouched.
